question.text: Under FATCA and CRS, AIFs as Reporting Financial Institutions must comply with which Indian tax rules and register with which authority?

answer.text: Rules 114F-114H of the Income Tax Rules, 1962; register with US IRS for GIIN AND with Indian Income Tax authorities
Rule 10 of FEMA; register only with RBI
Rule 20 of SEBI ICDR; register with SEBI only

explanation.text: The Logic: FATCA and CRS compliance for AIFs is operationalised in India via Rules 114F to 114H of the Income Tax Rules, 1962. AIFs must register with the US IRS to obtain a GIIN (Global Intermediary Identification Number) and with the Indian Income Tax authorities. FATCA self-declaration from Indian and NRI investors has been mandatory from January 2016. The Trap: Options B, C and D cite the wrong regulatory frameworks. FEMA, SEBI ICDR and the Companies Act do not house FATCA/CRS — the Income Tax Rules do. Note: Workbook pages 387-388 support the FATCA/CRS rule, the registration requirements and the January 2016 self-declaration mandate.
